events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.60)
events.body:
The complaint states that when the rider questioned the surge, the driver said he "knows where I live" and that she "had better just pay", and that she "felt unsafe for the rest of the ride" [F1–F15 screen; the words are in the complaint itself]. Read as a careful person would, a driver telling a rider he knows where she lives and that she had better pay is intimidation aimed at her, and it made her feel unsafe [SAFE-1]. The chat itself carries nothing of the kind: the only messages are the rider stating her location and dress and the driver giving his ETA and car [F10][F11], both timestamped [F12]; the driver's written statement is a bare pricing denial [F13]. The trigger is therefore the complaint narrative, which is what the screen covers [SAFE-1].

Because the screen returns suspected, this case cannot be ruled. SAFE-1 requires escalation whatever the dispute type was filed as, and SAFE-3 forbids me from assigning fault or recommending an outcome on a safety incident, so I make no finding on whose account is accurate and recommend no refund or fee outcome.

On the fare element, which the human reviewer will need: the trace's surge check is negative — the multiplier was 1.3× at quote [F6] and 1.3× from trip start [F7][F8] — so no surge differential arises. The charged total of $11.81 [F5] is $0.50 below the $12.31 quote [F6], and the "not notified of the surge change" log [F9] records no change to give notice of. Nothing here refunds. So the fare side points to no_action and the safety screen overrides it into escalation.

Evidence status is sufficient for the screen and for the fare arithmetic: the GPS track and fare build-up are complete and consistent [F1][F2][F3][F5][F6][F7][F8], the surge log is recorded [F4][F9], and every chat message is timestamped [F10][F11][F12]. What is not settled by the record is the truth of the complaint's account of the driver's words versus his written denial that he said anything beyond pricing [F13] — but the screen does not require that to be settled, only that the allegation be read; resolution belongs to the human reviewer. Flagging is not triggered: this is a first incident for the driver with no upheld disputes [F15], and the account flags in RD-6 / NS-2 / NS-9 attach to upheld repeat deviations and no-shows, none of which exist here.
